limitations: 功能摘要根据作者固定版本材料归纳，不是逐字引文或独立效果验证。

findings.text: 监督式计算研究中管理反复变化的假设、代码数据、作业和论文依据。见 [Q01](#research-q01)。
DSH工具/角色接Kernel，BFF做人类Gate，Kernel限定合同/Protocol和Runner，作业manifest再进入Evidence接受链。见 [Q02](#research-q02)、[Q03](#research-q03)。
深查DSH工具ACL、人类Gate BFF/内部门禁、full-auto allowlist、正式提交/Runner物化/完成与Evidence接受。未全审所有Kernel/连接器/OCR/写作、Docker参数及SSH/GPU身份；未运行目标。
根包0.1.0，BSD-3-Clause，private源码工作区插件加独立UI；作者要求构建并声明未发布@dsh-scholar包。

| 依赖或条件 | 是否必需 | 用途 | 缺失或不满足时 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Linux/Node24/pnpm11.20 | 本地工作台必需 | 构建与运行 | 不按作者支持环境使用 |
| Kernel/BFF及各类身份凭据 | 必需 | 持久状态与Human批准 | 内部写接口拒绝 |
| Runner Profile/Target | 作业必需 | 执行环境和能力 | 未登记/离线/不匹配拒绝 |
| 固定Docker镜像 | 正式作业必需 | 隔离与重建环境 | 禁止退宿主子进程 |
| 模型/OCR/检索/SSH/GPU | 特定路径 | 研究扩展与计算 | 另有费用及部署验收 |

| 阶段 | 现金与资源成本 | 人工与时间投入 | 已知条件与未知项 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 首次使用 | 服务/镜像/存储未知 | 构建部署、迁入合同数据 | 需容器维护能力 |
| 持续使用 | 模型/OCR/算力未知 | Gate、证据和版本维护 | 未测总项目收益 |
| 失败恢复 | 重跑/保存快照未知 | 查租约/manifest、恢复备份 | 远程故障未全验 |
| 退出 | 持久项目仍占空间 | 保留原数据、CAS、TeX再卸载 | 不把移除UI当删/备份项目 |
保留浏览器token，在监督且隔离的本地环境用已知fixture试gate-only；先故意未批/缺metrics核拒绝与终态，异常备份Kernel和原数据回独立脚本。--no-token仅属受限开发例外。见 [Q05](#research-q05)。

| 效果项 | 当前证据支持 | 尚不能确定 |
|---|---|---|
| 批准治理 | BFF身份到事务Gate | 所有部署安全 |
| 正式运行 | 合同/Protocol及租约绑定 | 远程SSH/GPU实效 |
| 证据追溯 | manifest/作业/合同重验 | 科学结论有效性 |
| 工作组织 | 责任与材料同项目 | 人工负担和总成本改善 |
内部服务凭据与浏览器身份分离、CAS输入和租约完成、Evidence再验可借鉴；仍须把可追溯与科学正确分开。见 [Q02](#research-q02)、[Q03](#research-q03)。
将批准责任、不可变输入、租约作业与证据验收串成持久项目；这是工程与工作组织增量，非自动科学发现的验证。见 [Q02](#research-q02)至[Q04](#research-q04)。
full-auto只执行限定fixture的survey_run，来源已验不代表科学正确；部署身份、远程隔离和人类复核负担仍决定价值。见 [Q02](#research-q02)至[Q04](#research-q04)。
以版本差异视图减少Human Gate重复阅读，同时不漏掉代码/数据/指标变化；现有UI已等效或误批增加就推翻。见 [Q05](#research-q05)。

technical.rationale: [Q02](#research-q02)、[Q03](#research-q03)把现成身份/事务/CAS/租约组合成研究语义边界，相对散脚本novelty50%、mechanism50%，未比较直接完整平台不达75%。决策、运行和证据分离有可迁移的接口与契约，transferability50%，超过仅局部便利的25%；但迁入其他受控计算的身份、数据和admission规则仍需适配，未核直接替代关键限制及主要反例，不支持75%。[Q04](#research-q04)组件多且增加治理负担，simplification25%，未达50%。

business.rationale: [Q04](#research-q04)把审批、执行和证据接受责任分开，workflow50%，不只是入口；Evidence/manifest作为可验交付delivery50%，科学结论仍人负责，无直接替代效果不达75%。需容器与科研方法技能，未识别新受限群体进入机制，reach0。就本次核查的贡献而言，Runner仍消费现有Docker/模型/存储资源，合同和Gate改变验收责任，已计workflow/delivery，未识别资源池化、采购计价或服务交付经济结构增量，economics0；这是当前已识别机制的归因判断，不是因未量化ROI而以0代未知。若后续发现资源复用或调度经济机制，应另核比较。

recommendation.reason: 能维护本地容器的计算研究者可保留浏览器 token，用已知结果的非敏感 fixture 试用 gate-only 流程。相对散落的脚本和笔记，它绑定合同、输入和证据，但必须监督批准并独立判断实验结论。若作业终态或证据关联不清，应停止自动推进、备份项目并回独立脚本和人工证据账本。

scenario.rationale: [Q01](#research-q01)、[Q04](#research-q04)反复改输入/批准/验收造成可追溯性摩擦，明确监督研究者为何承担负担，超过50%用途明确，达75%；无真实持续采用材料不达100%。

advantage.rationale: [Q02](#research-q02)身份与批准、[Q03](#research-q03)合同/metrics/Evidence的实际拒绝链相对散脚本改变验收，超过50%入口便利达75%；完整平台对照和科学效果未测不达100%。

evidence.rationale: [Q02](#research-q02)、[Q03](#research-q03)固定server/kernel/runner链支持local fixture有条件试用，达50%；未运行和远程身份未全审，不达75%。

cost.rationale: [Q04](#research-q04)需部署多服务、容器、凭据和人工Gate，已有数据备份/退出退路但恢复边界未全核，25%；尚不足50%负担已可控。

publication.summaries.text: 计算研究工作台，将项目对话、资料、受控实验、证据关系与 TeX 写作放在持久项目中。

items.模型工具: 项目、方法论、实验、证据和写作入口
items.用户命令: 研究阶段与项目控制命令
items.界面: DSH紧凑页与独立研究工作台

publication.capabilities.table:
| 能力 | 主要用途 | 使用条件与边界 |
|---|---|---|
| 角色工具ACL | 约束阶段Agent | 依赖宿主执行前钩子 |
| Human Gate | 人批准研究决策 | BFF身份/成员/CSRF及service凭据 |
| full-auto | 固定fixture受限推进 | 自动动作仅survey_run，非无人论文 |
| 合同/Protocol作业 | 绑定输入和执行环境 | 正式作业要求冻结批准 |
| Runner完成 | 回传manifest/metrics | exit0不自动成功 |
| Evidence接受 | 重验来源/作业/合同 | 不证明科学正确 |
| 研究工作台 | 查看项目/运行/TeX等 | 非所有路径已独立验证 |

publication.advice.text: 保留浏览器token，在监督且隔离的本地环境用已知fixture试gate-only；先故意未批/缺metrics核拒绝与终态，异常备份Kernel和原数据回独立脚本。--no-token仅属受限开发例外。见 [Q05](#research-q05)。

      "path": "README.md",
      "content": "# DSH Scholar\n\n[简体中文](README.zh-CN.md) | **English**\n\nDSH Scholar is an AI research workspace for computational research. It keeps project conversations, research materials, code and data, controlled experiment runs, evidence, and TeX manuscripts in one recoverable project. You can start from a new question or continue work that already exists elsewhere.\n\n> DSH Scholar is still under active development. Use it for supervised computational-research workflows, review every approval and research claim, and keep independent backups of important source material and results.\n\n![DSH Scholar standalone workspace in English](docs/assets/dsh-scholar-home-en.png)\n\n## What it provides\n\n- **Stage-aware research guidance**: Chat supports natural conversation, Grill Me intake, file upload, visual-model input, explicit slash commands, and an authoritative next-step prompt for the current research stage.\n- **Governed research workflow**: Scope, Idea, Contract, Evidence, Direction, and Release decisions remain explicit, revision-bound, and auditable.\n- **Controlled execution**: Runner Profiles describe local, local-Docker, or remote-SSH environments, including pinned container images and declared NVIDIA GPU capability.\n- **Integrated workspace**: project-scoped Chat, editable files, session-bound Web terminals, run logs, artifacts, TeX source, compilation diagnostics, and PDF preview share the same context.\n- **Traceable methodology**: Protocol revisions, run classifications, synthesis requests, assurance results, reviewer findings, knowledge-pack activation, and claim-to-evidence links are recorded as durable research state.\n- **Visible collaboration**: Trajectory and Topology expose subagent parent-child relationships, status, follow-ups, and outputs.\n\n## Intended use and boundaries\n\n- DSH Scholar assists researchers; it does not assume responsibility for scientific judgment, approval, authorship, or publication.\n- `gate-only` is the normal mode. Agents cannot impersonate a Human principal, fabricate accepted Evidence, or bypass a research Gate.\n- `full-auto` means automatic approval only for the allowlisted Scope, Idea, Contract, and Budget Gates of an exact registered FixtureProfile. Its only canonical action executor is currently `survey_run`. Release, Direction, Intake, Evidence, and unsupported actions remain Human-controlled or are parked with a typed reason.\n- A name-only `/new <name>` project always starts as `gate-only` and collects its Brief through Grill Me; it does not silently inherit `full-auto`.\n- Formal experiments must bind immutable code and data snapshots, a frozen Protocol where required, and an explicit Runner Profile. Chat text, ordinary stdout, and Interactive Terminal output do not automatically become formal Evidence.\n- Images sent to a visual model are untrusted, current-turn Chat context. They do not automatically become OCR output, Brief answers, Evidence, Claims, Gate decisions, or proof that a command ran.\n- The product focuses on computational research such as machine learning, data science, and bioinformatics. It is not intended for clinical decisions, human studies, wet-lab work, or other high-risk research.\n\n## Quick start\n\nThe local workspace requires Linux, Node.js 24, pnpm 11.20.0, and Docker Engine for controlled experiments, TeX compilation, and clean-room reproduction.\n\n### 1. Install and build\n\n```bash\npnpm install --frozen-lockfile\npnpm run build\n```\n\n### 2. Start the standalone workspace\n\n```bash\nbash scripts/start-standalone-ui.sh\n```\n\nOpen <http://127.0.0.1:18610> and paste the token from:\n\n```text\n~/.dsh-scholar-standalone/research-ui-standalone/standalone-token\n```\n\nThe standalone workspace and DSH use the same Research Kernel at `127.0.0.1:7412` and the same canonical project data directory at `~/.dsh/research-kernel`. Upgrading either surface must keep that directory unchanged so existing projects remain accessible. Browser tokens and display preferences live separately in the standalone BFF directory. Use `--no-token` only on an isolated, supervised, loopback-only development instance.\n\n### 3. Configure an execution environment\n\nOpen **Settings → Execution environment** and select an explicit Runner Profile:\n\n- local machine for trusted development and smoke checks;\n- local Docker with a pinned image, optionally requiring the NVIDIA runtime and GPU capability;\n- remote SSH with server-side endpoint, credential, known-hosts, and target-identity SecretRefs.\n\nFormal Jobs do not execute until the selected profile and target pass readiness checks. A missing Runner, offline target, unavailable SecretRef, capability mismatch, or incomplete Contract/Protocol is shown as preparation or a blocker instead of being treated as ready. See the [runtime guide](docs/test-instance-plan.md) for target registration, target-scoped heartbeat credentials, Runner startup, ports, and security constraints.\n\n### 4. Install the plugin in DSH\n\nInstall the current DSH prerelease through its moving `next` tag, then record the exact installed version:\n\n```bash\nnpm install -g @deepseek-ai/dsh@next\nnpm ls -g @deepseek-ai/dsh --depth=0\n```\n\nThe `@dsh-scholar/*` packages are not published yet. Build this repository and add its absolute path to DSH's `web` profile:\n\n```bash\ncd /absolute/path/to/dsh-scholar\npnpm install --frozen-lockfile\npnpm run build\ndsh plugin --profile web add /absolute/path/to/dsh-scholar\ndsh plugin --profile web why @dsh-scholar/research-plugin\ndsh web\n```\n\nTo update Scholar, rebuild this same checkout and add the same absolute path again. To uninstall it:\n\n```bash\ndsh plugin --profile web remove @dsh-scholar/research-plugin\n```\n\nThe plugin adds Scholar tools, slash commands, Skills, settings, and a compact `dsh Scholar` tab. An unlinked DSH conversation can bind an existing project or create a name-only project. A linked conversation shows only its current stage, next action, and execution summary; use **Open in new page** or the configured shortcut for the complete workspace.\n\n## Plugin configuration\n\nOpen **Settings → Plugin config → dsh Scholar** in DSH. Saved plugin changes take effect after the next DSH restart.\n\n| Setting | Default | Meaning |\n|---|---|---|\n| Default governance mode | `gate-only` | Applies only when a fully configured project explicitly qualifies for that mode. Name-only creation remains `gate-only`. |\n| Unattended runs | Off | Does not bypass Human Gates; an interaction requirement parks the project. |\n| Standalone URL | `http://127.0.0.1:18610/` | Target for **Open in new page** and the shortcut. Only HTTPS or loopback HTTP is accepted. |\n| Open-page shortcut | `Alt+Shift+S` | Can be disabled and does not fire while typing or using an IME. |\n\nWhen `full-auto` is enabled for a valid fixture, Settings also reports worker state, restart-required state, the fixture-only boundary, and the latest park reason. Release remains Human-controlled. The Standalone URL cannot contain credentials, query parameters, or fragments. **Copy standalone access token** is available only from a loopback DSH instance after an explicit click; the page never displays the token and does not expose Kernel, Runner, Provider, or SSH secrets.\n\n### Visual models in Chat\n\nScholar reads the live model catalog from DSH instead of guessing capability from a model name. Configure the actual DeepSeek-compatible image endpoint as an image-capable catalog entry in the DSH profile:\n\n```yaml\n- id: llm-deepseek\n  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm-deepseek'\n  config:\n    models:\n      - id: your-vision-model\n        name: Your Vision Model\n        inputModalities: [text, image]\n```\n\nRestart DSH, choose the model marked with `👁` in Scholar, attach or paste PNG, JPEG, WebP, or GIF images, then send a normal-language Chat message. The same upload may enter project Intake, but its visual bytes are consumed only by that successful free-conversation turn. A text-only or undeclared model is rejected before provider network I/O; Scholar never silently falls back to a text answer.\n\n## Start or continue research\n\nChoose one of three entry points:\n\n1. **New research**: provide only a project name, then answer the Grill Me questions in Chat to complete the Brief.\n2. **Open an existing project**: continue its persisted stage, project conversations, files, tasks, runs, and methodology history.\n3. **Upload / join**: add papers, code, data, images, or logs and attach them to an existing stage. Uploaded material first enters isolated Intake and never becomes Evidence automatically.\n\nThe usual flow is:\n\n```text\nCreate or join → Grill Me → Scope → survey → Ideas → Baseline → Contract\n→ controlled Runs → classification and synthesis → Evidence and Claims\n→ TeX writing and review → private bundle → Human Release Gate\n```\n\nChat accepts ordinary natural language and top-level slash commands. Explicit commands are deterministic advanced entry points; prose is interpreted against the project's current authoritative `NextAction`. For example:\n\n```text\n/new  /status  /survey  /ideas  /ideas generate 3  /ideas select <idea_id>\n/gates  /contract  /run  /evidence  /claims  /write  /review\n/release-bundle  /release\n```\n\n`/run` executes only when its exact snapshots, Protocol, Runner, target, and budget are ready. `/release` creates or opens a Human Release decision; it does not let an Agent publish automatically.\n\n## Example workflow\n\nThe repository includes a supervised MNIST handwritten-digit workflow that demonstrates project intake, controlled Docker runs, evidence review, and manuscript-ready results without treating the fixture as a benchmark claim.\n\n![MNIST project overview in English](docs/assets/cnn-mnist-actual-overview-en.png)\n\nSee the [MNIST reproduction guide](docs/mnist-reproduction.md) for the pinned inputs, rerun procedure, and detailed receipts.\n\n## Workspace areas\n\n| Area | Purpose |\n|---|---|\n| Chat | Natural conversation, Grill questions, uploads, visual-model input, command completion, and stage-aware guidance. |\n| Workspace | Browse, search, edit, upload, and manage project files with version/etag conflict protection. |\n| Run / Terminal | Inspect formal Job state and read-only logs, or operate a project/session-bound Web PTY. |\n| Evidence / Artifacts | Preview and download outputs, and review metrics, provenance, confidence, and claim links. |\n| Manuscript | Edit TeX, inspect compilation diagnostics, and preview the latest successful PDF generation. |\n| Trajectory / Topology | Inspect research history and enter subagent nodes to review their work and follow-ups. |\n| Settings | Configure model and OCR providers, MinerU, budgets, Runner Profiles, targets, Docker images, GPU requirements, and SSH SecretRefs. |\n\n## Validation boundary\n\nThe repository's automated acceptance covers builds, schemas, Kernel and Client behavior, governance and security regressions, persistence/restart behavior, DSH plugin contracts, visual-request admission with a controlled adapter, and controlled local-Docker fixtures. Real browser/ARIA observation, a clean DSH Host cold start, a production visual/reviewer provider, remote SSH/GPU execution, production mTLS termination, and environment-specific TeX rendering remain deployment-specific manual acceptance items. Check the [current implementation status](docs/hardening-v0.2-status.md) and [manual acceptance checklist](docs/manual-acceptance.md) before relying on those paths.\n\n## Documentation\n\n- [Usage guide](docs/USAGE_GUIDE.md)\n- [Runtime and deployment guide](docs/test-instance-plan.md)\n- [DSH host integration](docs/dsh-integration.md)\n- [Security and research-integrity baseline](docs/security-baseline.md)\n- [Acceptance specification](docs/acceptance-tests.md)\n\n## License\n\nThis project is licensed under the [BSD 3-Clause License](LICENSE).\n"

ORDER BY created_at').all(projectId) as unknown as Array<{ body: string }>\n    return rows.map(row => JSON.parse(row.body) as import('@dsh-scholar/research-schemas').EvidenceItem)\n  }\n\n  /** Deterministic claim verification against evidence (design §4.7, §11.3). */\n  verifyClaim(input: {\n    claim_id: string\n    evidence_ids: string[]\n    analysis_artifact?: string\n    reason?: string\n  }): Claim {\n    const current = this.getClaim(input.claim_id)\n    // hardening EVID-01 + §6: only ACCEPTED evidence (draft_unverified →\n    // verified → accepted, the last step by a Verifier/Auditor) may support a\n    // claim; draft notes, legacy rows and worker-verified-but-not-accepted\n    // rows are all excluded from the verdict.\n    const resolved = input.evidence_ids\n      .map(id => this.listEvidence(current.project_id).find(e => e.evidence_id === id))\n      .filter((e): e is NonNullable<typeof e> => e !== undefined)\n    if (resolved.length === 0) {\n      throw new KernelError(422, 'no_evidence', `claim ${input.claim_id} has no resolvable evidence`)\n    }\n    const evidence = resolved.filter(e => (e as { provenance_status?: string }).provenance_status === 'accepted')\n    if (evidence.length === 0) {\n      // Resolvable but not accepted: the verdict is inconclusive with an\n      // explicit reason (no 422 — the ids exist, provenance is lacking).\n      const update = this.db.prepare('UPDATE claims SET body = ?, updated_at = ? WHERE claim_id = ?')\n      const currentBody = JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(current)) as Claim\n      const inconclusive: Claim = {\n        ...currentBody,\n        status: 'inconclusive',\n        history: [...(currentBody.history ?? []), { status: 'inconclusive' as Claim['status'], at: nowIso(), reason: 'requires accepted evidence (verified → accepted by Verifier/Auditor)' }],\n      }\n      update.run(JSON.stringify(inconclusive), nowIso(), input.claim_id)\n      return inconclusive\n    }\n    // v2 §13.5: deterministic strict rules. Default is inconclusive.\n    // supported requires: accepted evidence, effect size present, CI present,\n    // n >= contract minimum (n_seeds or run count), CI excludes zero, and\n    // effect direction consistent with the claim (no direction info -> at\n    // most inconclusive).\n    let status: Claim['status'] = 'inconclusive'\n    const conflicted = evidence.some(e => e.status === 'conflicted')\n    const complete = evidence.filter(e =>\n      e.result.effect_size !== undefined\n      && e.result.ci_low !== undefined && e.result.ci_high !== undefined\n      && (e.result.n_seeds ?? e.run_ids.length) > 0,\n    )\n    if (!conflicted && complete.length > 0) {\n      // §12 MetricSpec direction: lower-is-better inverts the sign\n      // interpretation — a NEGATIVE effect (CI < 0) is the improvement and\n      // supports the claim; a positive effect contradicts it. Evidence that\n      // declares no direction defaults to higher_is_better.\n      const directions = new Set(complete.map(e => e.result.direction ?? 'higher_is_better'))\n      const lowerIsBetter = directions.size === 1 && directions.has('lower_is_better')\n      const allCiExcludeZero = complete.every(e => e.result.ci_low! > 0 || e.result.ci_high! < 0)\n      const anyNegativeEffect = complete.some(e => (e.result.effect_size ?? 0) < 0)\n      const allPositiveEffect = complete.every(e => (e.result.effect_size ?? 0) > 0)\n      const allNegativeEffect = complete.every(e => (e.result.effect_size ?? 0) < 0)\n      if (allCiExcludeZero && lowerIsBetter) {\n        if (allNegativeEffect) {\n          status = 'supported'\n        } else if (allPositiveEffect) {\n          status = 'contradicted'\n        } else {\n          status = 'inconclusive' // mixed directions\n        }\n      } else if (allCiExcludeZero && allPositiveEffect) {\n        status = 'supported'\n      } else if (allCiExcludeZero && anyNegativeEffect && !allPositiveEffect) {\n        status = 'contradicted'\n      } else {\n        status = 'inconclusive' // CI crosses zero or mixed directions\n      }\n    }\n    const next: Claim = {\n      ...current,\n      evidence: { evidence_ids: input.evidence_ids, analysis_artifact: input.analysis_artifact ?? current.evidence.analysis_artifact },\n      status,\n      confidence: status === 'supported' ? 'high' : status === 'contradicted' ? 'high' : 'medium',\n      history: [...current.history, { status, at: nowIso(), reason: input.reason ?? `verified against ${evidence.length} accepted evidence item(s)` }],\n      updated_at: nowIso(),\n    }\n    this.db.prepare('UPDATE claims SET body = ?, updated_at = ? WHERE claim_id = ?').run(JSON.stringify(next), next.updated_at, input.claim_id)\n    this.emit(current.project_id, 'claim.updated', { claim_id: input.claim_id, status })\n    return next\n  }\n\n  createClaim(input: { project_id: string; statement: string; scope?: Claim['scope'] }): Claim {\n    this.getProject(input.project_id)\n    const claim: Claim = {\n      claim_id: buildClaimId(),\n      project_id: input.project_id,\n      statement: input.statement,\n      scope: input.scope ?? { dataset: '', split: '' },\n      evidence: { evidence_ids: [] },\n      status: 'proposed',\n      confidence: 'medium',\n      limitations: [],\n      history: [{ status: 'proposed', at: nowIso(), reason: '' }],\n      created_at: nowIso(),\n      updated_at: nowIso(),\n    }\n    this.db.prepare('INSERT INTO claims (claim_id, project_id, body, updated_at) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)')\n      .run(claim.claim_id, claim.project_id, JSON.stringify(claim), claim.updated_at)\n    return claim\n  }\n\n  getClaim(claimId: string): Claim {\n    const row = this.db.prepare('SELECT * FROM claims WHERE claim_id = ?').get(claimId) as { body?: string } | undefined\n    if (row?.body === undefined) throw new KernelError(404, 'claim_not_found', `claim ${claimId} not found`)\n    return JSON.parse(row.body) as Claim\n  }\n\n  listClaims(projectId: string): Claim[] {\n    const rows = this.db.prepare('SELECT * FROM claims WHERE project_id = ? ORDER BY updated_at').all(projectId) as unknown as Array<{ body: string }>\n    return rows.map(row => JSON.parse(row.body) as Claim)\n  }\n\n  // ── analysis pipeline (design §4.7, §11.3 Statistics) ────────────────────\n\n  /**\n   * Deterministic multi-seed analysis over succeeded formal runs: aggregate\n   * metrics from RunManifest metrics artifacts in CAS, compute mean, sd,\n   * percentile bootstrap 95% CI and effect size vs the baseline run. Writes\n   * one analysis artifact; numbers in manuscripts must come from this.\n   */\n  computeAnalysis(projectId: string, contractId?: string, metric?: string, options: {\n    /** Minimum completed seeds required (v2 §13.6; default 1 keeps compat). */\n    minimum_n?: number\n    /** Restrict to these job kinds (v2 §13.6: never mix kinds). Defaults to\n     * formal; falls back to non-baseline kinds only when no formal exists. */\n    kinds?: string[]\n  } = {}): {\n    artifact_id: string\n    chart_artifact: string\n    contract_id: string | null\n    metric: string\n    runs: Array<{ run_id: string; job_id: string; value: number; seed?: number }>\n    mean: number\n    sd: number\n    n: number\n    ci_low: number\n    ci_high: number\n    baseline_value: number | null\n    effect_size: number | null\n    used_kinds: string[]\n    generated_at: string\n  } {\n    const project = this.getProject(projectId)\n    const jobs = this.listJobs(projectId).filter(j => j.status === 'succeeded' && j.run_manifest !== null)\n    const metricValues: Array<{ run_id: string; job_id: string; kind: string; value: number; seed?: number }> = []\n    let baselineValue: number | null = null\n    let formalSeen = false\n    for (const job of jobs) {\n      if (contractId !== undefined && job.contract_id !== contractId) continue\n      if (job.kind === 'formal') formalSeen = true\n      const metricsArtifact = job.run_manifest?.metrics_artifact\n      if (typeof metricsArtifact !== 'string') continue\n      const sha = metricsArtifact.replace(/^sha256:/, '')\n      if (!this.cas.has(sha)) continue\n      // §12.5 (SCH-EXEC-002): metrics artifacts carry the fixed-schema file\n      // record ({schema_version, seed, metrics: [{name, value, unit}]});\n      // legacy stdout-derived artifacts used {metric, value, seed}. Both keys\n      // are accepted, and the §12.5 top-level `seed` is used as the per-entry\n      // fallback.\n      const parsed = JSON.parse(this.cas.read(sha).toString('utf8')) as { metrics?: Array<{ metric?: string; name?: string; value?: number; seed?: number }>; seed?: number }\n      for (const entry of parsed.metrics ?? []) {\n        const metricName = entry.name ?? entry.metric\n        if (entry.value === undefined || metricName === undefined) continue\n        if (metric !== undefined && metricName !== metric) continue\n        metricValues.push({\n          run_id: typeof job.run_manifest?.run_id === 'string' ? job.run_manifest.run_id : job.job_id,\n          job_id: job.job_id,\n          kind: job.kind,\n          value: entry.value,\n          seed: entry.seed ?? parsed.seed,\n        })\n        if (job.kind === 'baseline' && baselineValue === null) baselineValue = entry.value\n      }\n    }\n    // v2 §13.6: never mix job kinds. Prefer formal runs; only when a contract\n    // has none, fall back to the other non-baseline kinds (explicitly noted).\n    let allowedKinds = options.kinds ?? ['formal']\n    const hasFormal = formalSeen\n    if (options.kinds === undefined && !hasFormal) allowedKinds = ['pilot', 'smoke', 'analysis', 'reproduce']\n    // Baseline runs always stay in the set: they are the pairing side.\n    const kindFiltered = metricValues.filter(v => v.kind === 'baseline' || allowedKinds.includes(v.kind))\n    metricValues.length = 0\n    metricValues.push(...kindFiltered)\n    const usedKinds = [...new Set(kindFiltered.map(v => v.kind).filter(k => k !== 'baseline'))]\n    if (metricValues.length === 0) {\n      throw new KernelError(422, 'no_metrics', 'no succeeded runs with metrics artifacts found for analysis')\n    }\n    // §13.6 / STAT-01: THE analysis engine is the Analysis Worker's paired\n    // mean-difference (matched-seed design, seeded percentile bootstrap).\n    // The kernel never re-implements statistics — it collects baseline and\n    // treatment runs, pairs them by seed, and delegates the math.\n    // §12 MetricSpec direction + minimum_n: both resolved from the bound\n    // contract (explicit contract_id, else the project's first approved\n    // contract); direction defaults to higher_is_better, minimum_n to the\n    // contract's stop_conditions.min_completed_seeds (fallback 1) and a\n    // caller-lowered minimum_n is 422 (AnalysisPlan.minimum_n is\n    // contract-driven, reconstruction-contracts.md §12).\n    const approvedContracts = this.listContracts(projectId).filter(c => c.status === 'approved')\n    const boundContract = contractId !== undefined\n      ? approvedContracts.find(c => c.contract_id === contractId)\n      : approvedContracts[0]\n    let direction: 'higher_is_better' | 'lower_is_better' = 'higher_is_better'\n    if (boundContract !== undefined && boundContract.metrics.direction !== undefined) {\n      direction = boundContract.metrics.direction\n    }\n    const contractMinimum = boundContract?.stop_conditions.min_completed_seeds\n    const minimumN = options.minimum_n ?? contractMinimum ?? 1\n    if (contractMinimum !== undefined && options.minimum_n !== undefined && options.minimum_n < contractMinimum) {\n      throw new KernelError(422, 'minimum_n_too_low',\n        `analysis minimum_n ${options.minimum_n} < contract stop_conditions.min_completed_seeds ${contractMinimum} (cannot be lowered by the caller, §12)`)\n    }\n    const baselineRuns: Array<{ seed?: number; value: number }> = []\n    const treatmentRuns: Array<{ seed?: number; value: number }> = []\n    for (const v of metricValues) {\n      if (v.kind === 'baseline') baselineRuns.push({ seed: v.seed, value: v.value })\n      else treatmentRuns.push({ seed: v.seed, value: v.value })\n    }\n    // STAT-01 (P0): a seed that appears in MULTIPLE runs of the same group\n    // (baseline or treatment) makes the matched-seed design ambiguous — the\n    // old behavior silently overwrote/`find`-firsted it. Formal analyses now\n    // reject duplicate seeds outright (422 duplicate_seed): each baseline and\n    // each treatment seed must be unique across the collected runs.\n    const assertUniqueSeeds = (group: string, runs: Array<{ seed?: number }>): void => {\n      const seen = new Set<number>()\n      for (const r of runs) {\n        if (r.seed === undefined) continue\n        if (seen.has(r.seed)) {\n          throw new KernelError(422, 'duplicate_seed',\n            `${group} seed ${r.seed} appears in multiple runs — duplicate seeds are rejected in formal analysis (STAT-01); re-run with unique seeds`)\n        }\n        seen.add(r.seed)\n      }\n    }\n    assertUniqueSeeds('baseline', baselineRuns)\n    assertUniqueSeeds('treatment', treatmentRuns)\n    const baselineBySeed = new Map<number, number>()\n    for (const b of baselineRuns) {\n      if (b.seed !== undefined) baselineBySeed.set(b.seed, b.value)\n    }\n    const pairedSeeds = treatmentRuns\n      .filter(t => t.seed !== undefined && baselineBySeed.has(t.seed!))\n      .map(t => t.seed!)\n    const uniquePaired = [...new Set(pairedSeeds)]\n    if (uniquePaired.length < minimumN) {\n      throw new KernelError(422, 'matched_seeds_required',\n        `analysis requires >= ${minimumN} baseline/treatment runs with MATCHED seeds (paired design, §13.6); got ${uniquePaired.length}`)\n    }\n    const paired = uniquePaired.sort()\n    const baselineValues = paired.map(s => baselineBySeed.get(s)!)\n    const treatmentValues = paired.map(s => {\n      const hit = treatmentRuns.find(t => t.seed === s)!\n      return hit.value\n    })\n    const worker = this.analysisPort.computePaired(\n      {\n        contract_id: contractId ?? 'auto',\n        metric: { name: metric ?? 'auto', direction, aggregation: 'mean' },\n        paired_by: 'seed',\n        baseline_run_set_id: 'kernel-baseline',\n        treatment_run_set_id: 'kernel-treatment',\n        method: { estimator: 'paired_mean_difference', interval: 'bootstrap_95', resamples: ANALYSIS_RESAMPLES },\n        multiple_testing: 'holm',\n        minimum_n: minimumN,\n      },\n      paired.map((s, i) => ({ run_id: `baseline-${s}`, seed: s, metric_value: baselineValues[i]! })),\n      paired.map((s, i) => ({ run_id: `treatment-${s}`, seed: s, metric_value: treatmentValues[i]! })),\n    )\n    const mean = worker.treatment_mean\n    const variance = treatmentValues.reduce((acc, v) => acc + (v - mean) ** 2, 0) / Math.max(treatmentValues.length - 1, 1)\n    const sd = Math.sqrt(variance)\n    const result = {\n      contract_id: contractId ?? null,\n      metric: metric ?? 'auto',\n      direction,\n      runs: metricValues\n        .filter(v => v.kind !== 'baseline' && v.seed !== undefined && paired.includes(v.seed!))\n        .map(({ kind: _kind, ...rest }) => rest),\n      mean: round(worker.treatment_mean),\n      sd: round(sd),\n      n: worker.n_pairs,\n      ci_low: round(worker.ci_low),\n      ci_high: round(worker.ci_high),\n      baseline_value: round(worker.baseline_mean),\n      effect_size: round(worker.effect_size),\n      adjusted_p_value: round(worker.adjusted_p_value),\n      direction_ok: worker.direction_ok,\n    }\n    const artifact = this.registerArtifact({\n      project_id: projectId,\n      kind: 'analysis',\n      content: JSON.stringify({ analysis: result, method: 'percentile-bootstrap-95', n_resamples: ANALYSIS_RESAMPLES, project_id: projectId }, null, 2),\n      media_type: 'application/json',\n      file_name: 'analysis.json',\n      metadata: { kind: 'analysis', metric: result.metric, n: result.n, generated_by: 'research-kernel.computeAnalysis' },\n    })\n    this.emit(projectId, 'artifact.registered', { artifact_id: artifact.artifact_id, kind: 'analysis' })\n    // Deterministic chart artifact bound to the same analysis numbers (§11.3).\n    const chart = this.buildChartSvg(projectId, { artifact_id: artifact.artifact_id, ...result })\n    return { artifact_id: artifact.artifact_id, chart_artifact: chart.chart_artifact, used_kinds: usedKinds, ...result, generated_at: nowIso() }\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Generate a deterministic SVG bar chart for one analysis result (design\n   * §11.3 charts, E5): mean with bootstrap CI whiskers vs baseline. The SVG\n   * is registered as a `chart` CAS artifact so manuscripts embed artifact\n   * references, not ad-hoc numbers.\n   */\n  buildChartSvg(projectId: string, analysis: {\n    artifact_id: string\n    metric: string\n    mean: number\n    ci_low: number\n    ci_high: number\n    baseline_value: number | null\n    n: number\n  }): { chart_artifact: string; svg: string } {\n    this.getProject(projectId)\n    const W = 420, H = 260, M = { l: 60, r: 20, t: 30, b: 40 }\n    const values = [analysis.baseline_value ?? analysis.mean, analysis.mean]\n    const lo = Math.min(...values, analysis.ci_low)\n    const hi = Math.max(...values, analysis.ci_high)\n    const span = Math.max(hi - lo, 1e-9) * 1.25\n    const scale = (v: number): number => H - M.b - ((v - lo) / span) * (H - M.t - M.b)\n    const barW = 70\n    const bar = (x: number, v: number, color: string, label: string): string => {\n      const y = scale(Math.max(v, lo))\n      const h = Math.max(H - M.b - y, 1)\n      const textY = y - 6\n      return `<rect x=\"${x}\" y=\"${y}\" width=\"${barW}\" height=\"${h}\" fill=\"${color}\" rx=\"3\"/>\n        <text x=\"${x + barW / 2}\" y=\"${textY}\" text-anchor=\"middle\" font-size=\"12\" fill=\"#333\">${label}: ${v.toFixed(4)}</text>`\n    }\n    const ciY = scale(analysis.ci_high)\n    const ciH = Math.max(Math.abs(scale(analysis.ci_low) - scale(analysis.ci_high)), 1)\n    const meanX = M.l + barW + 50\n    const baselineX = M.l\n    const svg = `<svg xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/2000/svg\" width=\"${W}\" height=\"${H}\" viewBox=\"0 0 ${W} ${H}\">\n  <text x=\"${W / 2}\" y=\"20\" text-anchor=\"middle\" font-size=\"14\" font-weight=\"bold\">${escapeXml(analysis.metric)} — mean ± 95% bootstrap CI (n=${analysis.n})</text>\n  ${analysis.baseline_value !== null ? bar(baselineX, analysis.baseline_value, '#9aa5b1', 'baseline') : ''}\n  ${bar(meanX, analysis.mean, '#4c6ef5', 'treatment')}\n  <rect x=\"${meanX + barW / 2 - 3}\" y=\"${ciY}\" width=\"6\" height=\"${ciH}\" fill=\"#f03e3e\"/>\n  <text x=\"${meanX + barW / 2}\" y=\"${H - M.b + 18}\" text-anchor=\"middle\" font-size=\"11\" fill=\"#555\">analysis ${analysis.artifact_id.slice(0, 12)}</text>\n</svg>`\n    const record = this.registerArtifact({\n      project_id: projectId,\n      kind: 'chart',\n      content: svg,\n      media_type: 'image/svg+xml',\n      file_name: 'analysis-chart.svg',\n      metadata: { kind: 'chart', metric: analysis.metric, analysis_artifact: analysis.artifact_id },\n    })\n    return { chart_artifact: record.artifact_id, svg }\n  }\n\n  // ── manuscript & release bundle (design §4.8) ────────────────────────────\n\n  /** Deterministic manuscript draft from the read-only Evidence Ledger. */\n  buildManuscript(projectId: string, format: 'markdown' | 'latex' = 'markdown', includeLimitations = true): {\n    manuscript_id: string\n    format: string\n    text: string\n    artifact_id: string\n    claims_used: number\n    bibtex: string\n  } {\n    const project = this.getProject(projectId)\n    const claims = this.listClaims(projectId)\n    const evidence = this.listEvidence(projectId)\n    const contracts = this.listContracts(projectId)\n    const snapshots = this.listCorpusSnapshots(projectId)\n    const supported = claims.filter(c => c.status === 'supported')\n    const byEvidence = new Map<string, Claim[]>()\n    for (const claim of claims) {\n      for (const id of claim.evidence.evidence_ids ?? []) {\n        byEvidence.set(id, [...(byEvidence.get(id) ?? []), claim])\n      }\n    }\n    const evidenceRows = evidence.map(e => {\n      const claimsFor = (byEvidence.get(e.evidence_id) ?? []).map(c => c.claim_id)\n      return `| ${e.result.primary_metric} | ${e.result.value} | ${e.result.baseline_value ?? '—'} | ${e.result.effect_size ?? '—'} | ${e.result.ci_low ?? '—'}–${e.result.ci_high ?? '—'} | ${e.result.n_seeds ?? e.run_ids.length} | ${e.analysis_method} | ${claimsFor.join(', ') || '—'} |`\n    })\n    const lines: string[] = []\n    if (format === 'latex') {\n      lines.push('\\\\documentclass{article}', '\\\\usepackage{booktabs}', '\\\\begin{document}')\n      lines.push(`\\\\title{${escapeLatex(project.name)}}`, '\\\\maketitle')\n      lines.push('\\\\section{Abstract}')\n      lines.push(abstractText(project, supported))\n      lines.push('\\\\section{Methods}')\n      for (const contract of contracts) {\n        lines.push(`\\\\subsection{${escapeLatex(contract.methods.treatment)} vs ${escapeLatex(contract.methods.baseline)}}`)\n        lines.push(`Dataset: ${escapeLatex(contract.data.dataset_id)} (split ${escapeLatex(contract.data.split)}), primary metric ${escapeLatex(contract.metrics.primary)}, seeds ${contract.seeds.join(', ')}.`)\n      }\n      lines.push('\\\\section{Results}')\n      if (evidenceRows.length > 0) {\n        // LaTeX tabular rows: '&'-separated, en dashes as '--' (§14.3: the\n        // fixed build image must compile; raw unicode dashes break pdflatex).\n        const latexRows = evidence.map(e => {\n          const claimsFor = (byEvidence.get(e.evidence_id) ?? []).map(c => c.claim_id).join(', ') || '--'\n          const ci = `${e.result.ci_low ?? '--'}--${e.result.ci_high ?? '--'}`\n          return `${escapeLatex(e.result.primary_metric)} & ${e.result.value} & ${e.result.baseline_value ?? '--'} & ${e.result.effect_size ?? '--'} & ${ci} & ${e.result.n_seeds ?? e.run_ids.length} & ${escapeLatex(e.analysis_method)} & ${escapeLatex(claimsFor)}`\n        })\n        lines.push('\\\\begin{tabular}{llllllll}', '\\\\toprule', 'Metric & Value & Baseline & Effect & 95\\\\% CI & Seeds & Method & Claims \\\\\\\\', '\\\\midrule')\n        lines.push(...latexRows.map(r => `${r} \\\\\\\\`))\n        lines.push('\\\\bottomrule', '\\\\end{tabular}')\n      } else {\n        lines.push('No verified evidence items yet — results table intentionally empty.')\n      }\n      lines.push('\\\\section{Related Work}')\n      for (const paper of snapshots.at(-1)?.papers ?? []) {\n        lines.push(`\\\\cite{${paper.paper_id.replace(/[^a-zA-Z0-9]/g, '_')}} ${escapeLatex(paper.title)} (${paper.year ?? 'n.d.'}).`)\n      }\n      if (includeLimitations) {\n        lines.push('\\\\section{Limitations}')\n        for (const claim of claims) {\n          if (claim.limitations.length > 0) lines.push(`\\\\begin{itemize} ${claim.limitations.map(l => `\\\\item ${escapeLatex(l)}`).join(' ')} \\\\end{itemize}`)\n        }\n      }\n      lines.push('\\\\end{document}')\n    } else {\n      lines.push(`# ${project.name}`, '', '## Abstract', abstractText(project, supported), '', '## Methods')\n      for (const contract of contracts) {\n        lines.push(`### ${contract.methods.treatment} vs ${contract.methods.baseline}`, `- Dataset: ${contract.data.dataset_id} (split ${contract.data.split})`, `- Primary metric: ${contract.metrics.primary}`, `- Seeds: ${contract.seeds.join(', ')}`, `- Analysis: ${contract.analysis.effect_size}, ${contract.analysis.interval}, ${contract.analysis.multiple_testing}`)\n      }\n      lines.push('', '## Results')\n      if (evidenceRows.length > 0) {\n        lines.push('| Metric | Value | Baseline | Effect | 95% CI | Seeds | Method | Claims |', '|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|', ...evidenceRows)\n      } else {\n        lines.push('No verified evidence items yet — results table intentionally empty (evidence-first).')\n      }\n      lines.push('', '## Related Work')\n      for (const paper of snapshots.at(-1)?.papers ?? all numbers traceable to run manifests and analysis artifacts.',\n      release_gate: 'unapproved',\n      created_at: nowIso(),\n    }\n    const artifact = this.registerArtifact({\n      project_id: projectId,\n      kind: 'bundle',\n      content: JSON.stringify(bundle, null, 2),\n      media_type: 'application/json',\n      file_name: 'release-bundle.json',\n      metadata: { kind: 'release-bundle' },\n    })\n    return {\n      bundle_id: bundle.bundle_id,\n      artifact_id: artifact.artifact_id,\n      contents: ['project', 'contracts', 'jobs+manifests', 'artifacts', 'claims', 'evidence', 'corpus snapshots', 'ai_usage'],\n      release_gate: 'unapproved',\n    }\n  }\n\n  // ── paper reproduction (docs/reproduction-contracts.md §2/§4) ────────────\n\n  /** Resolve a reproduction's opaque target/profile binding and return the\n   * canonical EnvironmentLock pins. Callers use this both when storing a\n   * spec and immediately before starting an attempt, so a target changed in\n   * between cannot execute under a stale or fabricated environment lock. */\n  private pinReproductionEnvironment(\n    binding: ExecutionBinding | null,\n    environmentLock: EnvironmentLock,\n  ): EnvironmentLock {\n    const lock = EnvironmentLock.parse(environmentLock)\n    if (binding === null) {\n      if (lock.target_id !== '' || lock.target_revision !== '' || lock.target_hash !== '' || lock.runner_profile_id !== '') {\n        throw new KernelError(422, 'runner_target_binding_required',\n          'reproduction environment target/profile pins require an execution_binding')\n      }\n      return lock\n    }\n    const profile = getRunnerProfile(binding.runner_profile_id)\n    if (profile === null || !profile.enabled) {\n      throw new KernelError(422, 'runner_profile_unknown',\n        `runner profile ${binding.runner_profile_id} is not an enabled registered opaque profile`)\n    }\n    const target = this.listRunnerTargets().find(candidate => candidate.target_id === binding.target_id)\n    if (target === undefined) {\n      throw new KernelError(422, 'runner_target_unknown',\n        `runner target ${binding.target_id} is not a registered opaque RunnerTarget id`)\n    }\n    if (!target.enabled || target.draining) {\n      throw new KernelError(409, target.draining ?       "path": "src/plugin/acl.ts",
      "content": "/**\n * Per-role tool ACL (design §4.1 工具面原则, §1.3 Least privilege).\n * Every research tool declares its allowed roles; a `tools/pre-execute`\n * listener denies calls outside the caller's role. Scholar never executes,\n * Writer never writes evidence, Runner has no DSH credentials.\n * @module @dsh-scholar/research-plugin/acl\n */\n\nexport type ResearchRole =\n  | 'none'\n  | 'director'\n  | 'scholar'\n  | 'curator'\n  | 'idea-panel'\n  | 'architect'\n  | 'engineer'\n  | 'operator'\n  | 'statistician'\n  | 'writer'\n  | 'reviewer'\n  | 'auditor'\n\nexport const RESEARCH_ROLES: readonly ResearchRole[] = [\n  'none', 'director', 'scholar', 'curator', 'idea-panel', 'architect', 'engineer',\n  'operator', 'statistician', 'writer', 'reviewer', 'auditor',\n]\n\n/** Session-bound methodology entry points callable by the root DSH\n * conversation. They cannot name an arbitrary project; each resolves the\n * caller's persisted session link before any read or write. */\nexport const DSH_SESSION_METHODOLOGY_TOOLS = [\n  'research_methodology_status',\n  'research_assurance_run',\n  'research_protocol_record',\n  'research_synthesis_record',\n  'research_writing_review_record',\n  'research_knowledge_activate',\n  'research_knowledge_deactivate',\n] as const\n\n/** Tools that require an explicit DSH Host confirmation before execution. */\nexport const RESEARCH_HUMAN_CONFIRMATION_TOOLS = [\n  'research_knowledge_activate',\n  'research_knowledge_deactivate',\n  'research_assurance_run',\n] as const\n\n/** Canonical research tool names. Obsolete aliases are intentionally absent. */\nexport const RESEARCH_TOOLS = [\n  // Bounded native-DSH conversation façade. Public to every DSH role, but it\n  // only resolves the calling session and never grants a low-level capability.\n  'dsh_scholar',\n  'research_project',\n  'research_phase',\n  'research_gate_request',\n  'research_budget',\n  'research_status',\n  ...DSH_SESSION_METHODOLOGY_TOOLS,\n  'research_panel',\n  'literature_search',\n  'paper_resolve',\n  'corpus_snapshot',\n  'passage_lookup',\n  'idea_create',\n  'idea_compare',\n  'novelty_audit',\n  'experiment_register',\n  'experiment_submit',\n  'experiment_status',\n  'experiment_cancel',\n  'evidence_note_create',\n  'claim_create',\n  'claim_verify_request',\n  'analysis_request',\n  'workspace_snapshot',\n  'patch_apply',\n  'baseline_prepare',\n  'baseline_verify',\n  'test_run',\n  'manuscript_build',\n  'manuscript_review',\n  'release_bundle_request',\n  // ONBOARD-01 intake prepare surface (research-onboarding.md §2): agents\n  // may begin/stage/scan/propose; Human answers and adopt stay in the\n  // authenticated native question UI/BFF.\n  'research_intake_begin',\n  'research_intake_stage',\n  'research_intake_scan',\n  'research_intake_propose',\n] as const\n\n/** Tool surface per role (design §4.1 table) — canonical names only. */\nexport const ROLE_TOOLS: Record<ResearchRole, readonly string[]> = {\n  none: ['dsh_scholar', ...DSH_SESSION_METHODOLOGY_TOOLS],\n  director: ['research_project', 'research_phase', 'research_gate_request', 'research_budget', 'research_status', 'research_panel', 'release_bundle_request', ...DSH_SESSION_METHODOLOGY_TOOLS],\n  // ONBOARD-01 (research-onboarding.md §2): the researcher (scholar) role\n  // prepares intakes — begin/stage/scan/propose. There is no Human-answer or\n  // adopt tool: those actions belong to the Human PI via the\n  // authenticated BFF/UI (researcher/viewer/auditor project members are\n  // likewise 403 on the kernel's adopt route).\n  scholar: ['literature_search', 'paper_resolve', 'corpus_snapshot', 'passage_lookup', 'research_status', 'research_methodology_status', 'research_synthesis_record', 'research_intake_begin', 'research_intake_stage', 'research_intake_scan', 'research_intake_propose'],\n  curator: ['literature_search', 'paper_resolve', 'corpus_snapshot', 'passage_lookup', 'research_status'],\n  'idea-panel': ['idea_create', 'idea_compare', 'novelty_audit', 'literature_search', 'research_status'],\n  architect: ['experiment_register', 'research_status', 'research_methodology_status', 'research_protocol_record', 'experiment_status'],\n  engineer: ['workspace_snapshot', 'patch_apply', 'baseline_prepare', 'baseline_verify', 'test_run', 'research_status', 'experiment_status'],\n  operator: ['experiment_submit', 'experiment_status', 'experiment_cancel', 'research_status'],\n  statistician: ['evidence_note_create', 'claim_create', 'claim_verify_request', 'analysis_request', 'research_status', 'experiment_status'],\n  writer: ['manuscript_build', 'research_status', 'research_methodology_status', 'research_writing_review_record'],\n  reviewer: ['manuscript_review', 'claim_verify_request', 'research_status', 'research_methodology_status', 'research_writing_review_record'],\n  auditor: ['claim_verify_request', 'manuscript_review', 'research_status', 'research_methodology_status', 'research_writing_review_record'],\n}\n\n/** v2 §3.1: unknown/unregistered agents default to `none` (deny), NOT director. */\nexport const DEFAULT_ROLE: ResearchRole = 'none'\n\n/** Fail-closed project fence for stage-subagent tool calls. The child may\n * name its bound project explicitly, but may never use an arbitrary project\n * or job id to escape that scope. */\nexport async function stageProjectScopeDenial(\n  projectScope: string,\n  args: unknown,\n  projectForJob: (jobId: string) => Promise<string>,\n): Promise<string | undefined> {\n  const record = args !== null && typeof args === 'object' && !Array.isArray(args)\n    ? args as Record<string, unknown>\n    : {}\n  if (typeof record.project_id === 'string' && record.project_id !== '' && record.project_id !== projectScope) {\n    return 'stage subagent project scope does not match project_id'\n  }\n  if (typeof record.job_id === 'string' && record.job_id !== '') {\n    try {\n      if (await projectForJob(record.job_id) !== projectScope) {\n        return 'stage subagent project scope does not match job_id'\n      }\n    } catch {\n      return 'stage subagent job scope could not be verified'\n    }\n  }\n  return undefined\n}\n\n/** In-memory session → role registry (roles are set per session). */\nexport class RoleRegistry {\n  private readonly roles = new Map<string, ResearchRole>()\n\n  set(sessionId: string, role: ResearchRole): void {\n    this.roles.set(sessionId, role)\n  }\n\n  delete(sessionId: string): void {\n    this.roles.delete(sessionId)\n  }\n\n  get(sessionId: string | undefined): ResearchRole {\n    if (sessionId === undefined) return DEFAULT_ROLE\n    return this.roles.get(sessionId) ?? DEFAULT_ROLE\n  }\n\n  /** Whether the role may call one canonical tool. */\n  allows(role: ResearchRole, toolName: string): boolean {\n    return toolName === 'dsh_scholar' || ROLE_TOOLS[role].includes(toolName)\n  }\n}\n"

      "content": "/**\n * DSH Research OS — Cordis plugin entry (bundle: @dsh-scholar/research-plugin).\n *\n * Lifecycle (acceptance-tests.md §9, hardening §4 row 100):\n * 1. apply() is ASYNC and Cordis awaits it (cordis 4.0.0-rc.7 `_execute`\n *    collects a thenable apply result and `ctx.plugin()` resolves through\n *    `fiber.await()`, which waits for the fiber's reload task — so the plugin\n *    is only ACTIVE after apply settles). The kernel sidecar is started\n *    FIRST and awaited; only after `sidecar.start()` resolves are the client,\n *    `ctx.research` (with the RESOLVED endpoint — `port: 0` included), the\n *    research tool surface, direct slash commands and the skill packs\n *    registered. Nothing is published before the kernel is healthy, so a\n *    `port: 0` endpoint is always the real bound port and no tool/command\n *    ever sees an unresolved endpoint.\n * 2. Start failure: logged explicitly and rethrown — Cordis marks the fiber\n *    FAILED and unloads everything registered so far (at that point only the\n *    sidecar disposer), so no half-initialized resource survives.\n * 3. Disposal: every resource is owned by the plugin fiber's Cordis effect\n *    model and released on dispose/reload — `ctx.tools.register` /\n *    `ctx.commands.register` / `ctx.on` / `ctx.provide` / `ctx.plugin` all\n *    register effect disposers on the calling fiber (verified in\n *    dsh-tools/dsh-commands/dsh-scope/cordis sources), and the sidecar\n *    disposer (`ctx.effect`) is registered FIRST so even a dispose during\n *    the async startup stops the kernel. Reload unloads the old fiber\n *    (kills the old sidecar, unregisters tools/commands/listeners) before\n *    re-applying, so no duplicate registration or leaked listener survives.\n * 4. Instance closure: all mutable state (client, cache, RoleRegistry,\n *    tool context) lives in per-apply closures — there is no module-level\n *    mutable ref, so two plugin instances in one process never cross-talk.\n *\n * Security stance (§1.2, §4.9): no danger-full-access, no web_fetch, no MCP,\n * no cordis self tools. Default permission surface stays workspace-write + ask.\n * @module @dsh-scholar/research-plugin\n */\n\nimport type { Context } from '@deepseek-ai/cordis'\nimport z from '@deepseek-ai/schemastery'\n// Module augmentations: ctx.tools (ToolRuntime), ctx.commands (CommandRuntime).\nimport type {} from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools'\nimport type {} from for (const key of Object.keys(value)) {\n    if (!ROOT_CONFIG_KEYS.has(key)) {\n      issues.push({ message: `unknown config key \"${key}\"`, path: [key] })\n    }\n  }\n  if (isRecord(value.kernel)) if (typeof value.standalone.shortcut === 'string') {\n    try {\n      normalizeStandaloneShortcut(value.standalone.shortcut)\n    } catch (error) {\n      issues.push({ message: (error as Error).message, path: ['standalone', 'shortcut'] })\n    }\n  }\n  return issues\n}\n\n/**\n * Schemastery supplies the DSH config editor metadata and defaults. 0 requests an ephemeral loopback port.'),\n    dataDir: z.string().min(1).description('Directory containing kernel.db, CAS, runtime identity and token files.'),\n    token: z.string().min(1).role('secret').description('Optional initial Kernel bearer token; persisted in a 0600 token file.'),\n  }).default({} as never).description('Managed Research Kernel sidecar.'),\n  defaultMode: z.union(['gate-only', 'full-auto'] as const).default('gate-only')\n    .description('Default project governance mode;
